clue.text: Doctor in Leeds is disposed to play the hypocrite

indicators.note: in says the doctor's letters go inside the rearranged letters of the city's name
disposed in the sense of arranged or set out, so the letters of Leeds are laid out afresh

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A doctor working in Leeds is inclined to be two-faced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is disposed' rearranges the letters of LEEDS IS around the doctor's letters, which 'in' places inside. MB is the medical degree.
explanation.definitionFit: To dissemble is to hide one's true feelings behind a false front, which is what a hypocrite does.

clue.text: Tube containing a coin

indicators.note: containing says the pipe word wraps round the single letter

parts.note: a duct is a tube or channel

explanation.surface: A coin has got stuck inside a pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A ducat was a gold or silver coin used across medieval Europe.

clue.text: Issue upheld by teacher in the nursery?

indicators.note: in a down clue, being held up by something means sitting above it in the column

parts.note: seed means offspring or issue
BEd, Bachelor of Education, is a teacher's degree

explanation.surface: A child is lifted up by a teacher in the nursery class.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery is a plant nursery, not a children's one, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A bed of fine soil where seeds are sown is a plant nursery in miniature.

clue.text: In French art, a sensitive citizen

indicators.note: In puts the single letter inside the French verb form

parts.note: es is French for 'art' as in 'thou art' (tu es)
tender means sensitive or sore

explanation.surface: In French art, a citizen of delicate feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'art' is the old verb (thou art), not painting; in French that is ES. An East Ender is a resident of London's East End.
explanation.definitionFit: An East Ender is a resident of the East End of London, a particular kind of citizen.

clue.text: Musical antonyms? It's a matter of taste

explanation.surface: Opposites in music turn out to be down to personal preference.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitter Sweet is a Noël Coward operetta whose title joins two opposite words; a bittersweet flavour mixes both tastes.

clue.text: Husband abandoned goddess for a long time

indicators.note: abandoned says the letter for husband is dropped from the goddess's name

parts.note: Hera was the Greek queen of the gods

explanation.surface: A husband walked out on a goddess for ages.
explanation.definitionFit: An era is an age or extended period of history.

clue.text: In Balzac he appears to be inferior

indicators.note: In says the letters are found inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: In a Balzac novel, a certain character seems to be second-rate.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cheap is of poor quality, low-grade.

clue.text: Vehicle carrying article of little weight

indicators.note: carrying says the vehicle holds the article inside it

parts.note: a cart is a simple vehicle
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A vehicle carries some lightweight item.
explanation.definitionFit: A carat is a tiny unit of mass, 200 milligrams, used for gems.

clue.text: The City he left on attaining a level of responsibility

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London

explanation.surface: He quit the City on reaching a senior position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The City' is the financial district of London, whose postal district is EC.
explanation.definitionFit: An echelon is a rank or tier within an organisation.

clue.text: Unattainable hope conveyed to the papers

parts.note: piped means sent through a pipe, conveyed
a ream is a quantity of paper, 500 sheets

explanation.surface: A forlorn wish is passed on to the press.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipe dream is a fantasy that will never be realised.

clue.text: It holds a light cruciferous plant, it's said

parts.note: cress belongs to the cabbage family, Cruciferae

indicators.note: said signals that the little word is spoken and written as it sounds

parts.note: it is read as the plain pronoun, the 's joining it to the sound signal

explanation.surface: A light cress plant, people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a light' looks like it describes the plant, but it belongs to the definition: a cresset holds a flame.
explanation.definitionFit: A cresset is an iron basket or cup holding burning oil or coals as a beacon or torch.

clue.text: Position of one who is going to succeed, say, being a high-flyer

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase's word is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.words: Position of one who is going to succeed
parts.note: heirship is the status of an heir, who will succeed to a title

explanation.surface: Being next in line, you might say, makes someone a high achiever.
explanation.definitionFit: An airship is a dirigible balloon, literally something that flies high.

clue.text: Artist abandons first studies for a display of figures

indicators.note: abandons first says the painter's name drops its opening stretch

parts.note: John Constable was an English landscape painter
to con is to study, so cons are studies

explanation.surface: A painter gives up early sketches for a numerical exhibit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Artist' is a specific painter, Constable; 'studies' is not drawings but the verb con, to study.
explanation.definitionFit: A table sets out numbers in rows and columns.

clue.text: Met at Bled in formation, fortified against attack

indicators.note: in formation suggests troops being arranged, so these letters are lined up anew

explanation.surface: Gathered at Bled in battle order, defended against assault.
explanation.walkthrough: Bled is a lake resort in Slovenia; it is just fodder here.
explanation.definitionFit: Embattled originally meant prepared for battle, with battlements against attack.

clue.text: He may publicize players in a wider context

indicators.note: in says the actors' word sits inside the comparative adjective

parts.note: broader means wider
the cast are the players in a show

explanation.surface: Someone who promotes performers to a larger audience.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadcaster makes things public over radio or television.

clue.text: A young fellow located without one

indicators.note: without says the numeral letter is removed

parts.note: laid means placed or located
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A youth found on his own.
explanation.definitionFit: A lad is a boy or young man.

clue.text: Some try to earn their living in them

definitions.text: Some try to earn their living in them

parts.words: Some try to earn their living in them
parts.note: reads like strivers in a workplace, but 'try' means conduct a trial: judges and barristers make their living hearing cases

explanation.definitionFit: Courts of law are where judges try cases and lawyers earn fees.

clue.text: Abandon party in tune with development

parts.note: a disco is a dance party

indicators.note: development means working the letters into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Give up the party once it is in harmony with progress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with development' rearranges the letters of IN TUNE; 'party' as a noun, a disco, comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: To discontinue is to stop doing or give up something.

clue.text: Urban view of Welsh opencast development

indicators.note: development means the letters are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: A city scene arising from Welsh mining.
explanation.walkthrough: Opencast mining digs coal from surface pits, a big industry in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: A townscape is the visual appearance of a town, or a picture of one.

clue.text: Flooded grassland where Wren originally made a tower, perhaps

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the architect's name
perhaps hints that the letters could form something else

explanation.surface: Christopher Wren once built a tower on a soggy field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' takes the first letter of Wren; 'perhaps' rearranges MADE A TOWER into ATERMEADOW to follow it.
explanation.definitionFit: A water meadow is pastureland deliberately flooded by a nearby river to enrich it.

clue.text: Animal climbing on part of roof perceived by touch

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means the word reads upwards

parts.note: a cat is an animal
a tile is part of a roof

explanation.surface: A cat climbing up the roof tiles, felt by hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' reads the animal upwards, as a down clue goes, sitting on the roof part below it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tactile means relating to the sense of touch.

clue.text: One who is relatively silent?

parts.note: 'relatively' points to a family relative, a mother, while the same word means saying nothing

explanation.definitionFit: Mum is a mother, a relative, and 'keep mum' means stay quiet.

clue.text: Second consignment of vermouth primarily for his cocktail

parts.note: mo is short for moment, a second
a lot is a batch of goods

indicators.note: primarily picks the opening letters of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: A second shipment of vermouth, mainly for his mixed drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The Molotov cocktail, a petrol bomb, is named after the Soviet minister.
explanation.definitionFit: The improvised firebomb is named after Vyacheslav Molotov, Soviet foreign minister.

clue.text: Container carried by odd Scottish players

indicators.note: carried by says the box sits inside the Scots word

parts.note: orra is Scots for odd or spare
a chest is a container

explanation.surface: A box carried by some unusual Scottish musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestra is a large group of musicians playing together.

clue.text: King holding decoration for a great diver

indicators.note: holding says the royal letters wrap round the award

parts.note: ER is Edward Rex, a king
MBE is an honour, Member of the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: A king hands out an honour for a champion swimmer.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'great diver' is a bird, the great northern diver (loon), also called the ember goose.
explanation.definitionFit: Ember goose is an old name for the great northern diver, a seabird.

clue.text: Sound form of geometry

explanation.surface: A reliable shape in geometry.
explanation.definitionFit: Solid means sound or dependable; a solid is a three-dimensional figure such as a cube.

clue.text: Shoots game

explanation.definitionFit: Darts means shoots or dashes; darts is the pub game of throwing at a board.

clue.text: Illusory hope chased by a cockney painter?

definitions.text: Illusory hope chased by a cockney painter?

parts.words: Illusory hope chased by a cockney painter?
parts.note: people chase an impossible goal at the end of the sky's arch

explanation.definitionFit: Chasing a rainbow means pursuing an unreachable dream.

clue.text: Court deal, say, almost completed

indicators.note: almost completed means the timber word stops one letter short

parts.note: deal is a type of softwood, an example of timber

explanation.surface: A trade agreement is nearly finalised in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deal' is pine timber, not a bargain; 'Court' is the verb to woo.
explanation.definitionFit: To court someone is to pursue them romantically.

clue.text: Casement, possibly, in characteristic gold

parts.note: a trait is a characteristic
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A window frame, perhaps, in a typical golden style.
explanation.walkthrough: Casement is Sir Roger Casement, hanged for treason in 1916, not a window.
explanation.definitionFit: Roger Casement was executed as a betrayer of Britain for aiding German-backed Irish rebels.

clue.text: Guide prophet across square

indicators.note: across says the seer is spread across the letter, enclosing it

parts.note: a seer is a prophet
a T-square is a drawing tool, so T stands for square

explanation.surface: A prophet leads people across the town square.
explanation.definitionFit: To steer is to direct or guide.

clue.text: We emphatically sue lovers, oddly enough

indicators.note: oddly enough suggests the letters are in a strange order

explanation.surface: We really do take our partners to court, strange as it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: Ourselves is the emphatic form of 'we', as in 'we did it ourselves'.
